causal:influence:aldolase_b_activity:neg.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 15 (fructose catabolism: KHK → F1P; ALDOB cleaves F1P); Scriver's OMMBID (hereditary fructose intolerance, OMIM 229600 — fructosuria is a diagnostic feature after fructose/sucrose ingestion); Harrison's Principles (HFI: nausea, hypoglycemia, fructosuria after fructose intake). | intervention: ALDOB loss-of-function (HFI, OMIM 229600): do(aldolase_b_activity↓) → fructose-1-P accumulates → fructose backs up → urinary_fructose↑

ALDOB LoF (hereditary fructose intolerance, HFI, OMIM 229600) → fructose-1-P accumulates in hepatocytes → fructose cannot be cleared (KHK product inhibition and direct fructose backup) → plasma fructose rises → fructosuria. ALDOB activity ↑ → fructose-1-P cleared → fructose catabolism proceeds → urinary fructose ↓.

causal:influence:alpha_galactosidase_a_a.mechanism: RHEA:48020 (EC 3.2.1.22): a globoside Gb3Cer (CHEBI:88154) + H2O = a beta-D-galactosyl-(1->4)-beta-D-glucosyl-(1<->1)-ceramide (LacCer) + D-galactose; Gb3Cer (globotriaosylceramide) is the primary substrate

causal:influence:amyloid_protein_aggrega.evidence: PMC8543248 — 'NLRP3 Inflammasome: A Starring Role in Amyloid-β- and Tau-Driven Pathological Events in Alzheimer's Disease'; PMC6231249 — 'Amyloid β directly interacts with NLRP3 to initiate inflammasome activation'; PMC3877570 — 'Oligomeric amyloid β induces IL-1β processing via production of ROS: implication in Alzheimer's disease'; APP/PSEN1 transgenic mice lacking NLRP3 show reduced Aβ deposition and IL-1β, confirming the causal chain (PMC12009708). | intervention: do(amyloid_protein_aggregate_amount↑) — as occurs in Alzheimer's disease (APP, PSEN1/2 gain-of-function mutations; APOE4 risk allele); also modeled by Aβ oligomer injection or APP/PS1 transgenic mouse overexpression
causal:influence:amyloid_protein_aggrega.mechanism: Amyloid-beta oligomers and fibrils activate microglial NLRP3 inflammasome through multiple convergent pathways: (1) Aβ binds CD36, triggering TLR4-TLR6 heterodimer → NF-κB → pro-IL-1β and NLRP3 transcription; (2) Aβ disrupts lysosomal integrity → cathepsin B release → NLRP3 priming; (3) Aβ oligomers directly bind NLRP3/ASC; (4) Aβ-driven mitochondrial ROS → NLRP3 activation → caspase-1 cleavage of pro-IL-1β → mature IL-1β secretion. Net effect: Aβ aggregate accumulation raises circulating and brain-resident IL-1β.

causal:influence:aprt_activity:negative:.evidence: APRT deficiency OMIM 614723 (2,8-dihydroxyadenine urolithiasis); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, purine salvage pathways; Edvardsson et al., Am J Kidney Dis 2013 (APRT deficiency: 2,8-DHA produced by XO from unsalvaged adenine). | intervention: do(APRT LoF, OMIM 614723) — adenine not salvaged, oxidized by XO to 2,8-dihydroxyadenine
causal:influence:aprt_activity:negative:.mechanism: APRT salvages adenine (with PRPP) back to AMP; in APRT deficiency, free adenine is not salvaged and is instead oxidized by xanthine oxidase sequentially to 8-hydroxyadenine and then 2,8-dihydroxyadenine (2,8-DHA), which is insoluble and causes urolithiasis. More APRT activity = less free adenine = less 2,8-DHA produced.

causal:influence:arterial_compliance:neg.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-112 (20.3: Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance): 'A persistently high pulse pressure at or above 100 mm Hg may indicate excessive resistance in the arteries'; arterial stiffening reduces the ability to buffer systolic pressure surges.
causal:influence:arterial_compliance:neg.mechanism: A compliant artery absorbs the stroke volume ejected per beat, dampening the systolic pressure rise; reduced compliance causes the same stroke volume to produce a larger systolic spike and thus wider pulse pressure

causal:influence:asns_activity:positive:.evidence: Asparagine synthetase deficiency (OMIM 615574); PMC4486270 — 'asparagine synthetase deficiency: new inborn errors of metabolism; CSF asparagine concentration is typically low or not detected; plasma asparagine concentration is low in about half of affected individuals'; GeneReviews NBK525916 — 'low CSF asparagine supports the diagnosis'; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (asparagine biosynthesis via ASNS). | intervention: do(ASNS activity ↓) = asparagine synthetase deficiency (OMIM 615574)

Reduced ASNS activity → less asparagine produced → plasma (and especially CSF) asparagine falls (∂[Asn]/∂(ASNS activity) > 0).

causal:influence:bace1_activity:positive.evidence: PMID 27807285; (Abstract; Sci Transl Med 2016;8:363ra150); “verubecestat (MK-8931) is a potent, selective, structurally unique BACE1 inhibitor that reduced plasma, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and brain concentrations of Aβ40, Aβ42” | Inhibiting BACE1 lowers Abeta concentrations, so do(BACE1 up) raises Abeta and its aggregate burden: BACE1 activity --(+)--> amyloid. Pharmacological BACE1 inhibition (verubecestat) is a do(BACE1 down) that lowers CNS/CSF Abeta.

causal:influence:bace1_activity:positive.evidence: Mechanism: BACE1 is the rate-limiting beta-secretase generating Abeta40; BACE1 inhibitors dose-dependently lower CSF Abeta (pharmacological do()). causal:influence:bace1_activity:positive.mechanism: Amyloid-beta 40 is generated by sequential cleavage of APP by beta-secretase (BACE1) then gamma-secretase. Abeta40 is the dominant, relatively soluble, less aggregation-prone Abeta species; its CSF concentration tracks amyloidogenic production, and pharmacological BACE1 inhibition lowers CSF Abeta40 dose-dependently. Higher BACE1 activity -> more Abeta40 production -> higher CSF Abeta40. Mirrors the curated edge bace1_activity -> csf_amyloid_beta (+).

causal:influence:beta_glucuronidase_acti.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 7 (GAG catabolism; beta-glucuronidase role); Sly syndrome / MPS VII OMIM 253220; Neufeld & Muenzer in Scriver's Metabolic Bases: GUSB deficiency causes storage of HS, DS, and CS; urinary HS is a sensitive marker; all three GAGs accumulate in MPS VII | intervention: do(GUSB activity ↓) = Sly syndrome / MPS VII (OMIM 253220): urinary heparan sulfate, dermatan sulfate, and chondroitin sulfate elevated

causal:influence:beta_ureidopropionase_a.evidence: Beta-ureidopropionase deficiency OMIM 613161; van Kuilenburg et al., J Inherit Metab Dis 2008. | intervention: do(UPB1 LoF, OMIM 613161) — N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine rises in urine
causal:influence:beta_ureidopropionase_a.mechanism: Urinary N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine is the same compound as ureidopropionate (3-ureidopropionate = N-carbamoyl-beta-alanine = CHEBI:18261); UPB1 deficiency causes this metabolite to accumulate in urine.

causal:influence:biotinidase_activity:po.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (biotin recycling by biotinidase); OMIM 253260 (biotinidase deficiency); Harrison's, 'Vitamin deficiency'

causal:influence:bmp_smad_signaling:posi.evidence: Ganz & Nemeth 2011 (Annu Rev Med 62:347-360); Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (hepcidin/BMP-SMAD regulation). causal:influence:capillary_hydrostatic_p.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-113 (20.4: Capillary Exchange): 'The net filtration pressure (NFP) represents the interaction of the hydrostatic and osmotic pressures, driving fluid out of the capillary. causal:influence:capillary_permeability:.evidence: SP-D traverses disrupted alveolar-capillary barriers proportionally to surface-area loss, mirroring albumin leakage; serum SP-D rises in ALI/ARDS due to barrier injury and leakage into circulation. causal:influence:cox_1_activity:positive.mechanism: Platelet COX-1 (PTGS1) converts arachidonic acid to PGH2, which is then converted by thromboxane synthase to TXA2; TXA2 spontaneously hydrolyses to stable TXB2 (the measured plasma analyte). causal:influence:cpt2_activity:negative:.mechanism: CPT2 cleaves oleoylcarnitine (C18:1, oleic acid ester of carnitine) to regenerate oleoyl-CoA and free carnitine inside the mitochondrial matrix; reduced CPT2 activity accumulates oleylcarnitine in plasma

causal:influence:csf_dihydrobiopterin:po.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (BH4 regeneration by dihydropteridine reductase, QDPR); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (BH4 salvage)
causal:influence:csf_dihydrobiopterin:po.mechanism: 7,8-dihydrobiopterin (BH2) is reduced to tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) by dihydrofolate reductase / dihydropteridine reductase; more substrate (BH2) supports more BH4 regeneration (product formation, salvage limb)

causal:influence:csf_dopamine:positive:c.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (catecholamine biosynthesis: dopamine --DBH--> norepinephrine); DBH deficiency OMIM 223360 — undetectable norepinephrine and epinephrine in plasma/CSF, dopamine accumulation; Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine (dopamine-beta-hydroxylase deficiency). | intervention: do(DBH LoF) — dopamine-beta-hydroxylase deficiency
causal:influence:csf_dopamine:positive:c.mechanism: Dopamine beta-hydroxylase (DBH) hydroxylates dopamine to norepinephrine in noradrenergic and adrenergic neurons; dopamine in the CNS is the direct substrate of DBH, so the CSF dopamine pool co-determines CSF norepinephrine. DBH deficiency (OMIM 223360) abolishes norepinephrine while dopamine accumulates.

causal:influence:csf_guanidinoacetate:po.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (creatine biosynthesis: AGAT then GAMT); Blau et al., Physician's Guide to Inherited Metabolic Diseases (cerebral creatine-deficiency syndromes: GAMT, AGAT)
causal:influence:csf_guanidinoacetate:po.mechanism: guanidinoacetate is methylated by GAMT to creatine; more guanidinoacetate substrate supports more creatine (product). causal:influence:cystathionine_gamma_lya.mechanism: CTH cleaves cystathionine to cysteine + 2-ketobutyrate + NH₃; 2-ketobutyrate is then transaminated by branched-chain aminotransferases to alpha-aminobutyrate (2-aminobutyrate). Higher CTH activity drives more 2-ketobutyrate and more alpha-aminobutyrate (∂[AABA]/∂(CTH activity) > 0). CTH deficiency → less 2-ketobutyrate → plasma alpha-aminobutyrate falls.

causal:influence:d2hgdh_activity:positiv.evidence: D-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria type I (D2HGDH deficiency, OMIM 600721): Struys et al.
